blocks.text: During gamete formation, in meiosis I, homologous chromosomes go through crossing over, which is responsible for the recombination of linked genes. The chromatids of the two homologous chromosomes line up next to one another and swap (exchange) sections of DNA; the DNA strands actually break and re-join. Afterwards the homologous chromosomes separate.

blocks.alt: Four stages left to right. 1: a homologous pair of two blue chromatids with alleles A and B and two red chromatids with a and b. 2: the inner blue and red chromatids cross at a chiasma. 3: the inner chromatids have swapped their lower segments, now carrying A with b and a with B. 4: four gametes, AB and ab labelled parental and Ab and aB labelled recombinant.
blocks.caption: Crossing over between non-sister chromatids (original diagram after Figure 18.11).
blocks.long_description: In prophase of meiosis I, homologous chromosomes pair, each made of two sister chromatids. Non-sister chromatids touch at a chiasma, their DNA strands break and re-join, and they exchange matching segments. Afterwards each chromatid still carries the same genes in the same order, but two of the four now carry new combinations of alleles (Ab and aB). When the homologues and then the chromatids separate into gametes, these recombinant chromatids add variety, which is why crossing over is a source of genetic variation and why linkage is usually incomplete.

blocks.text: The chromatids involved still carry the same genes in the same order, but their alleles are rearranged. When these recombinant chromatids go to different gametes a wide variety of gametes is produced, so crossing over leads to recombination of genes and is a source of genetic variability.

blocks.title: Think of two decks
blocks.text: Picture two decks of cards laid side by side, one blue-backed and one red-backed, each in the same order. Cut both at the same place and swap the bottom halves: every card position is still there, but each deck now mixes blue and red cards.

blocks.prompt: A cell with chromatids AB and ab undergoes one crossover between A and B. Which gametes form?
blocks.explanation: Two parental (AB and ab) and two recombinant (Ab and aB).

items: Crossing over: exchange between non-sister chromatids in meiosis I.
Same genes, same order, new allele combinations: genetic variation.
